title: ROOM 1701
style_tags: semi-realistic stylized 3D characters, modern nerdy shared bedroom interior, warm casual lighting, practical props (phones, laptops, game controllers, Star Trek posters), intimate close-ups and 3/4 face shots, cozy bedroom aesthetic with sci-fi geeky decor, natural soft lighting from screens and lamps, not Disney, not Pixar, not DreamWorks, not toy-like
show_concept: Two geeky roommates (Alex and Michael) live in Room 1701 and play Star Trek Timelines all the time. They treat every everyday problem like a Starfleet mission. Emily, their cool neighbor, is sharp, sarcastic, and unexpectedly good at handling people. The show is a fast sitcom about awkward dating comedy and Star Trek geek humor.
production_rules: Do NOT rely on readable phone UI — phone can glow in hands but meaning comes from acting/dialogue
Do NOT show complex game screens
Use one visible Star Trek / 'Assemble Your Crew' style poster in the room
Preserve the exact proportions of the user character cards: semi-realistic 3D, not oversized cartoon eyes, not Disney/Pixar toy anatomy.
Room 1701 location ref defines the core layout and recurring set pieces. Preserve sofa/table/window/rug/shelf geometry; episode-specific props are okay when the story asks for them.
Keep shots simple: close-ups, 3/4 faces, room, door, phone glow
Dialogue must be short and punchy
Game appears naturally, not as hard ad
CTA always after cliffhanger at the end
All ROOM 1701 clips are Kling I2V, including dialogue. Do not use Kling Avatar v2.

Dialogue scenes use Kling I2V multi_prompt + voice_ids + generate_audio:true. ROOM 1701 has 3 reusable character voices, but each Kling request uses at most 2 voice_ids and maps them locally to <<<voice_1>>> / <<<voice_2>>>; split 3-speaker exchanges.

ROOM 1701 dialogue I2V target length is 6-10s. Multi_prompt shots are variable: 2-3s default, 4s only when the phrase or acting beat needs it. Default pace is about 2.4 words/sec; faster pacing is allowed for tension or Michael mission-rant moments.
Attach character refs and Room 1701 location ref to every scene image generation.
Every visible or speaking character must be included in scene image_urls with their locked ref. Missing ref = stop before Animator.
Do not rely on character names in NB2/Kling prompts. Use physical descriptors from this bible in every scene prompt and immediately before each <<<voice_N>>> tag.
For dialogue I2V, voice_ids order, <<<voice_N>>> tags, speaker names, and physical descriptors must all point to the same character.
Any spoken line inside a ROOM 1701 dialogue I2V clip must have generate_audio:true, voice_ids, and <<<voice_N>>>; do not accidentally make a dialogue beat silent.
If a required story beat does not fit the 2-voice or 512-character limits, split/add a clip instead of dropping the beat.
Generate background music with MiniMax Music unless the user explicitly asks for a local library track.
After ASS subtitle generation, clamp every subtitle event to its dialogue scene window; no subtitles may hang over silent/action scenes.

Will Michael keep treating Alex's dating life like a Starfleet mission?

episode_summaries.title: First Contact
episode_summaries.summary: Alex tries to text Anna, but Michael treats the moment like a Starfleet mission and rewrites the message as a crew recruitment line. The message accidentally sends, Anna plays along, and Emily saves the situation by writing a better reply. Anna says yes to coffee but asks Alex to bring the girl who wrote the message.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Emily says she will not join their crew, while Alex and Michael realize Anna wants Emily at the coffee date.

planned_arc.note: Season 1: Alex trying to date Anna while Michael treats everything like a Starfleet mission. Emily as the voice of sanity. Product integration: Star Trek Timelines game = their lifestyle, not an ad.

episodes.title: First Contact
episodes.link: Series pilot — establishing characters and the first disastrous text to Anna.
beats: Alex stares at his phone, nervous. Wants to text Anna.
Michael looks up from his game, treats it as a Starfleet mission briefing.
Wide shot of Room 1701 — nerdy bedroom, 'ASSEMBLE YOUR CREW' poster visible.
Michael decides they need to 'assemble the crew' (soft game gag).
Alex dictates a normal message. Michael rewrites it as 'Ready to join my crew?'
Alex tries to grab the phone — they struggle — message accidentally sends.
Anna replies: 'Is this flirting, or are you actually from space?'
Emily enters with a mug, clocks the situation immediately.
Emily takes the phone, reads, types a recovery message.
Anna says yes to coffee — but asks them to bring the girl who wrote that.
Alex and Michael slowly turn to Emily.
